top.title: Dialysis scandal: No patient has ever been dialysed on mats, floor – LUTH CMD
top.description: By Chioma Obinna & Blessing Oghene The Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) yesterday dismissed as false a viral social media video alleging that patients were being subjected to dialysis treatment on mats and floors at its facility, insisting that no patient had ever received such treatment at the hospital. Chief Medical Director of LUTH, Prof. Wasiu Adeyemo, who gave the clarification during a media briefing and tour of the hospital’s Lion Isaac Olusola Dada Dialysis Centre and Renal Institute in Lagos, described the allegation as misleading and damaging to the hospital’s reputation. Adeyemo expressed disappointment that a major television station broadcast the video without first contacting the hospital to verify the claims or obtain its response. “Nothing in LUTH is hidden. That’s why we showcase our activities every day, and you have access to us. It is quite unfortunate that somebody put something on social media and a major news outlet publicised it without contacting us,” he said. He insisted that the video had nothing to do with LUTH. “For the avoidance of doubt, that viral video has nothing to do with Lagos University Teaching Hospital. It is not LUTH. It could not have been LUTH,” he declared. The CMD disclosed that the hospital currently operates 16 functional dialysis machines, with capacity for 30, providing round-the-clock haemodialysis services to adult and paediatric patients. According to him, the centre recorded approximately 12,500 haemodialysis sessions between January 2022 and October 31, 2026, averaging 2,500 sessions annually and more than 200 monthly. He added that the cumulative downtime of the centre during the period was less than one per cent. Also speaking, Consultant Nephrologist and Deputy Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee, Prof. Taslim Babawale Bello, described the allegation as medically and technically unfounded, explaining that the dialysis centre was not an admission ward but a specialised facility where patients receive treatment for three to four hours before returning home or to their wards. “It is technically impossible to dialyse a patient on the floor. The dialysis machine requires a specially constructed tubing system to connect to the patient, and its length is limited,” Bello explained. He said strict hygiene and infection-prevention protocols were observed at the centre, adding that even visitors were required to observe protective measures before entering the dialysis area. Bello explained that the centre, which commenced operations in its present building in October 2021, was part of a specialised kidney care complex housing outpatient nephrology clinics, a dedicated pharmacy, laboratory services, consultants’ offices and a kidney transplant facility. He added that the centre had two specialised water treatment units to ensure that water used during dialysis was purified to the required standards. top.title: Jerry Jones gives emotional tribute to Martha Firestone Ford
top.description: DETROIT — Among the many tributes to longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford, legendary Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones shared a touching personal story the day after her death at 101 . Jones recalled a trip to Detroit in the early 2000s during the country's financial crisis, which rocked the automobile industry. Ford famously declined a bailout from the U.S. government, but it still was a tough time for the company. "I'll never forget her, her eyes were teared up, seriously," Jones said Wednesday, Nov. 25, on NFL Network's "Good Morning Football. "I remember her talking about what a hard time it had been. The Ford family had taken all of their stock to the bank to borrow money to keep Ford going during a hard time in this country and a hard time in the automobile business. "And I'll never forget her talking about the rough time it was for her, the disappointing time, because the team wasn't playing well, and how special Detroit is." The Lions announced the death of Firestone Ford on Tuesday night, Nov. 24. A member of the famous Firestone (tires) family, she married into the famous Ford (cars) family in 1947, when she wed William Clay Ford. The Fords became majority owners of the Lions in 1963, and Firestone Ford became principal owner following the death of her husband in 2014 at age 88. Firestone Ford remained principal owner until 2020, when she passed the baton to daughter Sheila Ford Hamp. But Firestone Ford remained heavily involved with the team, regularly attended practices and games. She attended a game at Ford Field as recently as this month. Jones, who bought the Cowboys in 1989, called Firestone Ford a heavily involved owner. "With all of that legacy, here she is, so sensitive, so involved in what we're doing in the NFL. She was great. She attended most of the meetings that I've attended over the last 30 years," Jones said on "Good Morning Football" on Wednesday. "And it was just an inspiration to see that beautiful lady on the other side of the room. I was a real admirer of her, and we're going to miss her." "I'll never forget her." Jerry Jones reflects on Martha Firestone Ford's lasting legacy and the impact she made on the Detroit Lions organization ❤️ pic.twitter.com/wyjifvEHf9 — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) November 25, 2026 All of the NFL's teams put out statements of condolences following Firestone Ford's death, as did Detroit mayor Mary Sheffield and governor-elect Jocelyn Benson. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and wife Jane also paid tribute in a statement Tuesday. The Goodells said: "Martha was special. She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions — and the game of football — better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor." top.title: Fisilau starts as England change five for All Blacks rematch
top.description: Greg Fisilau has made impressive replacement appearances over the past three weekends [Getty Images] Hard-hitting back row Greg Fisilau will make his first England start in one of five changes to their XV to face New Zealand. The Plymouth-born 23-year-old, whose father Keni was a Tonga international, has impressed off the bench in each of England's previous three wins this autumn. He brings an industrious carrying option to a back row that relies heavily on Ben Earl in that aspect of the game. Ben Curry's breakdown skills have been sacrificed to make space, with the Sale man relegated to the bench. Exeter's Fisilau has carried more than any other player in the Prem this season, as well as sitting fourth in the top-flight's tackle standings. Elsewhere Freddie Steward's good form is rewarded with a start ahead of George Furbank at full-back, while Tommy Freeman returns on the wing for Saturday's rematch (16:40 GMT). Freeman missed last weekend's 37-12 victory over the All Blacks with a minor thigh issue which forced his withdrawal in the hours before kick-off. Ellis Genge comes into the starting front row after a string of barnstorming performances across the latter half of England's Nations Championship campaign. He is joined in the front row by Luke Cowan-Dickie, who is preferred at hooker to Jamie George. Northampton's 21-year-old scrum-half Archie McParland, who made his debut off the bench against Japan a fortnight ago, is among the replacements once again. With less than a year until the Rugby World Cup, England head coach Steve Borthwick's auditions for fringe squad members are taking on more importance. Victory would ensure an autumn clean sweep, a sixth win in succession and a third-place finish in the overall standings of the inaugural Nations Championship. A win would also contribute to the northern hemisphere's points tally in a Ryder Cup-style competition which runs throughout the three days of action at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham. The tournament is being held every other year between Rugby World Cups and British and Irish Lions tours in an attempt to bring more of a narrative to the Test calendar and draw in fans. Six Nations holders France and world champions South Africa will contest Sunday's grand final (16:40 GMT). top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has told Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs that “margin for error simply does not exist” in the conduct of the 2027 General Elections. This was as he set six operational priorities for the RECs, from whom he said he expects “immediate, documented compliance and personal accountability.” Amupitan spoke on Wednesday in Abuja at a strategic consultative meeting with the RECs from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. Reviewing the off-cycle elections since he assumed office in October 2025, Amupitan said the exercises showed “what is achievable when planning starts early, logistics are properly sequenced, and supervision is hands-on.” They covered the governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, the FCT Area Council elections and sixteen legislative bye-elections. He said every bottleneck identified in the off-cycle reviews “must be permanently closed before Saturday’s nationwide simulation and well ahead of January 16.” He cautioned that “general elections operate on an entirely different magnitude and complexity.” The Commission, he said, is managing a verified register of over 100 million voters, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities who need accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “In an exercise of that scale, even minor administrative lapses in one state can trigger national headlines and cast doubt on otherwise solid work elsewhere. Margin for error simply does not exist. At this decisive stage of the electoral cycle, the calendar no longer allows for leisurely deliberation or deferred action,” he said. According to him, the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 177,299 polling units, followed on Saturday, February 6, 2027, by the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly polls. He described the RECs as “the Commission’s chief operational commanders in the field,” adding that the credibility and public legitimacy of the elections “rest squarely on the precision, vigilance, institutional neutrality, and administrative rigour” with which they lead their state offices. The first priority, he said, is the nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, in two polling units per ward. “It is a live operational stress test of our upgraded BVAS devices, our logistics workflows, and our automated result validation safeguards on the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” he said, referring to the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). top.title: A South Side Thanksgiving
top.description: We’re all thankful for Miguel Vargas and his ability to overcome adversity in his time with the Chicago White Sox. (And to be a great slugging duo with Munetaka Murakami!) | Getty Images Miguel Vargas gave White Sox fans something substantial to bring to the Thanksgiving table: A reminder that a player’s first impression does not have to become his final chapter. That is a sentiment worth sharing on the South Side this November. The White Sox finished 84-78, swept Houston in the Wild Card Series and pushed Cleveland to five games in the ALDS. The ending hurt. It should have. Caring enough about October baseball to be disappointed was itself something to appreciate. This Thanksgiving, I’m thankful for a team that gave us reasons to watch, reasons to argue and reasons to start sketching a 2027 lineup before the turkey was out of the oven. Gratitude still leaves room for expectations. Some of these players need to improve. Some might be elsewhere next season. Appreciating their contributions does not require promising everybody another seat. But this table has room for all 26 players on Chicago’s announced ALDS roster, minus new Colorado Rockie Davis Martin. Each gets a helping of thanks, some statistical stuffing and something to save room for next year. Miguel Vargas: A second helping of belief — The helping: I’m thankful that Vargas gave fans a reason to reconsider what they thought they knew. His combination of power and patience offers a useful model: damage matters, but so does declining a pitch you cannot damage. — The stuffing: 33 home runs and 101 walks. — Save room for pie: Another year of that discipline, with more opportunities to turn baserunners into runs. Munetaka Murakami: Something worth getting out of your seat for The helping: I’m thankful for the anticipation. A lineup needs players whose at-bats make you put down the remote, and Murakami supplied the power to demand that attention. The stuffing: 35 home runs in 127 games. Save room for pie: More contact without sacrificing the ability to change a game with one swing. His ceiling becomes considerably more interesting if fewer plate appearances end without a ball in play. Colson Montgomery: Power with unfinished business The helping: I’m thankful that Montgomery gives the White Sox a substantial offensive weapon at shortstop. His season also gives us a useful distinction: Appreciating what a young player can do while asking for more of what he still needs. The stuffing: 31 home runs, alongside 227 strikeouts. Save room for pie: Fewer empty swings. The power already earns a place at the table; improved contact could make the entire meal better. Chase Meidroth: Keeping the line moving The helping: I’m thankful for the player whose contribution does not require a towering fly ball. top.title: Aaron Rodgers requested Mike McCarthy be removed from relaying plays
top.description: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Pieces of the puzzle are coming together around the Steelers’ shocking decision to bench Aaron Rodgers. The Steelers released a statement, through their team spokesman Burt Lauten, that Mason Rudolph will start against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday. Rodgers won’t even dress and is already announced as inactive. NFL insider Mike Garafolo said on NFL Network that the Steelers were in the process of changing the delivery of their play calling duties to quarterbacks coach Tom Arth. “There was going to be a change in the process this week,” Garafolo said. “Tom Arth is the quarterbacks coach. He was going to be the one to radio the plays in to Rodgers. That change was that this was going to be how things were going to go for the entire game,” Garafolo said. “They worked through that at practice yesterday. They were also having meetings as late as 5:30- 6 o’clock to figure this stuff out.” “Rodgers was the one that wanted this change to be made and that’s why it was happening as early as the walkthrough yesterday,” Garafolo said. Rodgers took first-team reps on Tuesday and met with the media like any typical week. What happened between Rodgers talking and 11:10 p.m. Tuesday night? “Nobody was talking about Rodgers being benched so I do believe that it was late last night when Mike McCarthy finally made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers,” Garafolo said. “The question is, why?” Arth was the Steelers quarterbacks coach in 2025 when Rodgers joined the Steelers and was the only assistant coach to stay on staff when Mike McCarthy took over. nigeria.description: Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho has removed references to Aston Villa from his Instagram profile amid uncertainty over his future at the Premier League club. nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them. The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident. Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains. Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices. “For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said. When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise. “No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said. Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities. “People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said. He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom. According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support. “My finances were better before this government came in. nigeria.title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football. In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job. “It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.” The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last. “Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.” Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League. In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’” Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. nigeria.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country. Condemning the killings, Sani said Nigerians were more likely to support or excuse political violence when those attacked belonged to opposing political camps. “The political violence in Delta State has led to the death of four supporters of Senator Omo Agege of the NDC. A condemnable act. However, we are shying away from the truth that most Nigerians are fully in support of political violence as long as the victims are in the opposite camp,” he wrote. He argued that people who support violence against political opponents often fail to recognise that such acts could eventually affect their own side. “Most people encourage and support mob or thuggish acts against those they differ with in political choices or opinions. Those aiding and abetting political violence are feeding a Tiger with the thought that it will only consume their political adversaries,” Sani said. The former senator also criticised the media’s handling of reports of political attacks, accusing some media organisations of using descriptions that downplay the severity of violence depending on the political affiliation of those involved. Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining. He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment. “Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Next Technology (NXTT) Sells 500 Bitcoin to Fund AI Push Next Technology Holding (Nasdaq: NXTT) sold about 500 bitcoin last week and said it will put the money toward artificial intelligence projects, the latest public company to trim its bitcoin treasury as prices slide. The Japan-based software firm disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it sold the coins on Nov. 21 for about $29.22 million. That works out to an average price of $58,468.11 per bitcoin, net of fees and expenses. The sale leaves NXTT with 5,333 BTC. The company was paid in tether (USDT), the dollar-pegged stablecoin, rather than in dollars. NXTT said it plans to use the proceeds for research and development of its AI-related initiatives, including its AI software products and services, as well as for general corporate purposes. A shift away from buying The sale is the first under a program the company’s board approved on Oct. 30. That program allows NXTT to sell or pledge its bitcoin “from time to time in one or more tranches,” through exchange sales, block trades or loans that use the coins as collateral, with the stated aim of “reducing risk exposure and enhancing liquidity.” The filing also repeats a line from the company’s latest quarterly report that marks a clear break from its earlier approach. NXTT “does not currently expect to purchase additional Bitcoin,” the company said, adding that it has adjusted its strategy to focus on managing the coins it already holds. The program has no expiration date and doesn’t require the company to sell any set amount. The board can change, pause or end it at any time. As of Nov. 24, NXTT said it had not pledged any of its bitcoin as collateral. How NXTT built its stack NXTT, which is incorporated in Wyoming but based in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, describes itself as running two strategies: AI-enabled software development and holding bitcoin. It keeps substantially all of its coins with Japan-based institutional custodians, according to its quarterly filing . The company held 833 BTC at the end of 2024 and added 5,000 BTC in 2025, bringing its total to 5,833 BTC. Its filing puts the cost basis of those coins at about $183.1 million, or roughly $31,400 per bitcoin, meaning last week’s sale still came in well above what the company paid on average. Falling prices have still hit the books. NXTT reported a net loss of $32.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with net income of $295.1 million a year earlier. The company said the swing came mainly from a drop in the fair value of its digital assets. The company has also been reshaping its leadership around AI. Earlier this month it named Chan Phang Chuen, a former platform architect focused on computing infrastructure and AI inference, as chief technical officer after Hongliang Liu resigned from the role. Treasury firms turn sellers NXTT joins a growing list of public companies selling bitcoin to fund other businesses.

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets France’s Senate has rejected a proposal that would have forced bitcoin holders to report self-custody wallets worth €100,000 or more to the tax authorities, along with two other crypto tax measures in the 2027 budget. Senators voted down two identical amendments on Nov. 24 during debate on the first part of the 2027 finance bill. Both would have required taxpayers to declare crypto wallets they hold directly, outside a crypto service provider, when the total value inside reached at least €100,000 on Dec. 31 of the tax year. The first, amendment I-2447 , came from Sens. Pascal Savoldelli and Pierre Barros and the Communist-led CRCE-K group. The second, amendment I-2992 , came from Sen. Anne-Sophie Romagny and seven other senators. The government opposed both, and both were rejected. The case for a wallet rule in France Backers argued that France already makes taxpayers declare accounts on foreign crypto platforms, just like foreign bank accounts. Wallets that holders manage themselves, without an intermediary, escape any such obligation. “They have become the digital equivalent of the undeclared safe,” the CRCE-K group wrote in its amendment, adding that tax authorities can’t see them, check gains on them or reach them in an estate or when a holder moves abroad. Romagny’s version pointed to a gap in the numbers. Crypto holders in France realized €3.5 billion in gains in 2021, but only €400 million in digital assets were declared to the tax administration that same year, the amendment said. It proposed fines of up to €10,000 for failing to declare. The National Assembly had approved the same wallet rule on Nov. 3. It fell away the next day, when deputies rejected the entire revenue section of the budget. Senators then took up the same measure as an amendment to the budget. Stablecoin swaps and exit tax also rejected Senators also rejected two other proposals from the CRCE-K group. Amendment I-2421 would have ended France’s tax deferral on swaps into electronic money tokens under the EU’s MiCA rules. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? sports.title: Jerry Jones gives emotional tribute to Martha Firestone Ford
sports.description: DETROIT — Among the many tributes to longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford, legendary Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones shared a touching personal story the day after her death at 101 . Jones recalled a trip to Detroit in the early 2000s during the country's financial crisis, which rocked the automobile industry. Ford famously declined a bailout from the U.S. government, but it still was a tough time for the company. "I'll never forget her, her eyes were teared up, seriously," Jones said Wednesday, Nov. 25, on NFL Network's "Good Morning Football. "I remember her talking about what a hard time it had been. The Ford family had taken all of their stock to the bank to borrow money to keep Ford going during a hard time in this country and a hard time in the automobile business. "And I'll never forget her talking about the rough time it was for her, the disappointing time, because the team wasn't playing well, and how special Detroit is." The Lions announced the death of Firestone Ford on Tuesday night, Nov. 24. A member of the famous Firestone (tires) family, she married into the famous Ford (cars) family in 1947, when she wed William Clay Ford. The Fords became majority owners of the Lions in 1963, and Firestone Ford became principal owner following the death of her husband in 2014 at age 88. Firestone Ford remained principal owner until 2020, when she passed the baton to daughter Sheila Ford Hamp. But Firestone Ford remained heavily involved with the team, regularly attended practices and games. She attended a game at Ford Field as recently as this month. Jones, who bought the Cowboys in 1989, called Firestone Ford a heavily involved owner. "With all of that legacy, here she is, so sensitive, so involved in what we're doing in the NFL. She was great. She attended most of the meetings that I've attended over the last 30 years," Jones said on "Good Morning Football" on Wednesday. "And it was just an inspiration to see that beautiful lady on the other side of the room. I was a real admirer of her, and we're going to miss her." "I'll never forget her." NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and wife Jane also paid tribute in a statement Tuesday. The Goodells said: "Martha was special. The Philadelphia Eagles made notable changes to their offense in Sunday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Less play-action, more pistol. They changed up the basis of Sean Mannion’s offense, as 84% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps were in the shotgun and 64.2% involved motion — both were season-highs. A season-high 42% of plays were snapped between six and 10 seconds left on the play clock — far above the previous high of 24.2%. Play-action percentage — the basis of Mannion’s offense — was 8.0%. Since Joe Milton became the starting quarterback, the Eagles were trending in this direction. The results, unfortunately, have been more of the same. sports.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images Colin Cowherd believes two relatively unheralded players have transformed the Kansas City Chiefs. Neither Emmett Johnson nor Josh Downs arrived in Kansas City as established superstars, but both have made an immediate impact. Johnson was selected in the fifth round of this year’s NFL Draft and initially found himself behind Kenneth Walker in the running back pecking order. However, Walker has missed the last two games, allowing the rookie to step into a much bigger role and rush for 101 and 105 yards. His performances prove he can potentially handle the responsibility of a starting running back. Johnson also gives Kansas City another option alongside Walker, creating the possibility of a dangerous two-man rushing attack. Meanwhile, Downs arrived in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts , whereby the Chiefs sent a fourth- and fifth-round pick to strengthen their receiving corps. Cowherd believes the pair have helped turn Kansas City into a much more complete team. He said: “I think Emmett Johnson and Josh Downs are the real deal. And now they’ve got a highly mature, productive adult, a professional, in Josh Downs to rely on. sports.title: Real Madrid target Champions League top spot and €23 million windfall after perfect start
sports.description: Real Madrid target Champions League top spot and €23 million windfall after perfect start Following their 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday , Real Madrid have collected all 15 points from their opening five UEFA Champions League matches this season. As such, Los Blancos are now within touching distance of their first major objective: securing a place in the top eight and avoiding the additional knockout play-off round. Now, according to AS , with three league-phase fixtures remaining, Jose Mourinho’s side are also chasing a potential financial reward worth almost €23 million. Direct qualification to Round of 16 the main objective Five victories have put Real Madrid at the top of the league phase standings, although their position remains subject to PSG’s result later today. Nonetheless, the perfect start has placed them in a strong position to reach the Last 16 directly. However, it must be noted that previous editions of the competition have shown that 15 points are not necessarily enough to finish inside the top eight. Five wins in five games for Real Madrid in the Champions League. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) But, 16 points have proved sufficient to secure a place in the top eight, giving Real Madrid three more opportunities to reach the required total and potentially finish even higher. For Mourinho and his men, direct qualification for the Round of 16 would also mean avoiding an extra knockout tie in the midst of an already packed schedule. Since the new format was introduced, Real Madrid have failed to secure a top-eight finish and the Portuguese tactician remains determined to turn that around. Almost €23 million in additional prize money at stake There is also a substantial financial incentive attached to finishing at the top of the league phase standings for Real Madrid. The Merengues have already earned €10.5 million from their five victories, with UEFA awarding €2.1 million for each win. That comes on top of the €18.6 million guaranteed for participating in the league phase, taking the club’s current earnings in the competition to €29.1 million. Securing top spot would help the club rake in €23 million. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Finishing first would bring further rewards. UEFA’s distribution includes €275,000 for each position in the final league-phase ranking, meaning the team finishing at the top would receive €9.9 million. A further €2 million is awarded for finishing inside the top eight, while qualification for the round of 16 brings another €11 million. Combined, those potential payments amount to almost €23 million. Real Madrid have three matches left in their league-phase campaign, beginning with the trip to London to face Arsenal on 9 December. They will then return to the Bernabeu on 19 January to take on Austrian side LASK Linz before travelling back to London on 27 January to face Shakhtar Donetsk at Stamford Bridge.

Jacob Oram expects more bounce and movement in Christchurch than the Basin Reserve offered. Matt Henry says New Zealand will not try to predict the surface in advance. What Jacob Oram and Matt Henry expect from the Hagley Oval pitch in Christchurch The first Test of this series produced 1,327 runs for the loss of 24 wickets across five days, which is not the ratio either attack travelled to New Zealand expecting. Christchurch is supposed to be where that changes. Jacob Oram, New Zealand's bowling coach, made clear what the hosts are after when he spoke to reporters at the ground on Wednesday. "We're hoping that there's obviously a little bit more bounce and movement than we saw in Wellington," he said. He also warned against reading too much into the grass that will be left on the surface, which at Hagley Oval tends to look more threatening than it plays. Oram pointed out that it can dry out quickly once the match is under way. "It looks tough to start, but if you can get over that hump, then the batting becomes easier," Oram said, adding that New Zealand would not settle on their bowling plans until the morning of the match. Matt Henry struck a similar note at his own press conference in Christchurch, refusing to commit to any forecast of how the pitch will behave. "We don't have a crystal ball, so we don't know what it's going to be like," he said. The weather may decide it. Christchurch is forecast to be hot through the Test, which historically accelerates the drying process and flattens the surface out as the match goes on. Teams bowling first have won 10 Tests at Hagley Oval against four for sides batting first, which is the most lopsided split at any New Zealand venue and explains why the toss carries unusual weight here. Spin barely features. Pace bowlers account for roughly 90 percent of the wickets taken at the ground, with slow bowlers averaging around three wickets a Test, and that is before the breeze off the Southern Alps is taken into account. sports.title: Phillies lose polarizing free agent infielder to Royals on $20 million deal
sports.description: Phillies lose polarizing free agent infielder to Royals on $20 million deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies have been running it back for the last three years, and it's progressively gotten worse with each passing season. During the 2026-2027 MLB offseason, Dave Dombrowski and the Phillies know they need to make some changes, mainly to the starting lineup. While they've yet to make an addition, one change has already come to pass. According to Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic , the Kansas City Royals have reportedly agreed to a $20 million contract with free agent infielder Alec Bohm. His polarizing tenure in Philadelphia is now over, as he's headed to the AL Central this offseason. Phillies lose Alec Bohm to Royals with $20M reported deal "Free-agent third baseman Alec Bohm in agreement with Royals on a two-year, $20M contract, pending physical, source tells @TheAthletic," Rosenthal reported. While this isn't a roster move the Phillies are making this offseason, it's a very notable reported signing, as it means Bohm will officially not be coming back to Philadelphia in 2027. After spending the first seven years of his MLB career with the franchise, featuring some wild ups and downs, the Phillies and Bohm are headed different ways. Thanks to the Royals trading away Maikel Garcia, they needed infield help. While Bohm isn't of the same caliber as some of the other top options available this offseason, he's a solid veteran right-handed hitter who would be a nice pickup for a team. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news The Phillies had been trying to trade Bohm for two years before he left in free agency this offseason, but they couldn't find any takers. Now, he's joining the Royals, leaving the Phillies behind. A return to Philadelphia never seemed likely, not after the trade rumors over the past few years. But after the Phillies missed out on Teruaki Sato, there might've seemed to be a chance for the Phillies to turn back to their veteran infielder. Now, that's no longer possible, as Bohm is reportedly signing on with the Royals for $20 million over two years to likely fill in as their third baseman. Bohm posted 4.9 bWAR in seven seasons across 874 games played with 894 hits, 85 home runs, 483 RBI, and a 101 OPS+ to go with an All-Star nod and even a strong Home Run Derby run. It wasn't a perfect tenure in Philadelphia, and there were plenty of good and bad moments. As Bohm leaves the Phillies with a complicated legacy, the two sides are looking to the future without one another. technology.title: Lead azide detonation sends clouds over Iowa as questions of health risks swirl
technology.description: In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound. The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of less than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate. Local Iowa outlet KWQC caught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. technology.title: NASA's nuclear-powered Mars delivery service takes shape
technology.description: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October. Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars. There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design." The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth. Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate. Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit. Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space. NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module. "Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said. The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge . Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft. ESA is also targeting late 2028 for its long-delayed Rosalind Franklin rover. Missing the intended Mars departure opportunity could push SR-1 into a later launch window, although NASA has not specified a fallback schedule. ®

technology.title: Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away
technology.description: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons. Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved. The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window. Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142 The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote. Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums , where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair. Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate. Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things. For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window." Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong. The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

technology.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
technology.description: One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history : cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food. Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command. technology.title: JetBrains finds agents may cheat with open source
technology.description: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. technology.description: Unsurprisingly, we’re already seeing some solid Black Friday deals on a wide variety of e-readers. Everything from the Kobo Libra Colour to last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is on sale, but if you’re looking for something much cheaper — or considerably smaller — the Xteink X4 Classic is in a league of its own. Thankfully, the tiny e-reader is down to a new low of $54.87 ($55 off) at Amazon , making it an especially affordable alternative to Amazon’s latest Kindle. Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader Where to Buy: $109 $54.87 at Amazon (black) $109 $54.87 at Amazon (white) $109 $59 at Xteink The X4 Classic is an updated version of Xteink’s original pocket-sized e-reader, one that features a miniature 4.3-inch E Ink display that makes it more pocketable than any current Kindle or Kobo model. Like the pricier X4 Pro — which also happens to be on sale direct from Xteink for $84 — it features both physical page-turning buttons and magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones. At just 2.4 ounces and 4.9mm thick, it’s also easy to slip into a pocket, while its larger 920mAh battery can last up to 10 days on a single charge. That said, unlike the X4 Pro , the Classic lacks a touchscreen and built-in reading light, meaning you’ll need an external light to read in the dark. It also uses a proprietary magnetic charging connector instead of USB-C, and transferring books isn’t as straightforward as on a Kindle or Kobo. However, like the Pro, it does support the excellent CrossPoint Reader software , which you can install yourself to improve the reading experience. You can even use it to read books borrowed through Libby or purchased from stores like Kobo, though it takes a few extra steps to do so. Still, if you want an inexpensive, distraction-free way to read on the go, the X4 Classic is hard to beat for less than half the price of a Kindle. Read our hands-on impressions of the Xteink X4.

technology.title: Debian wakes up wearing Windows XP's actual skin
technology.description: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well. Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage , and X . Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO." It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway. Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. The top of the README warns: "This is a personal, experimental project, not a finished product for daily use." The developer has tested it only on a fresh Debian 13 installation and recommends a VM or spare machine, rather than an existing working desktop, which sounds like an excellent precaution to us. Also, before you ask, yes, it was vibe-coded with Claude. We found ourselves reminded of another crazy-but-is-it project that we wrote about back in January: What if Linux ran Windows... and meant it? Meet Loss32 . The Loss32 proposal was even more extreme. It suggested replacing essentially the entire Linux userland, so it would be a Linux kernel running Wine with a Windows desktop and Windows apps. However, Mikuta-san was way ahead of us – lower down, the README mentions and even links to Loss32. Saying that, since it launched at the end of 2025, the bottom of the Loss32 web page shows a couple of updates, reporting on delays in getting it working. That, to be honest, did not shock us, but we still admire the let's-do-this spirit. The developer also seems to have got slightly distracted by a previous project, touchHLE: high-level emulator for early iOS apps . Loss32, in turn, reminded us of Neptune OS, an attempt to give seL4 a Windows personality transplant . We wrote about that back in 2022, and work on it has continued: the project page shows updates in recent months. The team has also pushed out preview releases in 2022, 2024, 2025, and most recently in September. technology.title: Microsoft 365 Backup stretches recovery window to ten years
technology.description: Recovery windows of up to ten years are now available in Microsoft 365 Backup for OneDrive and SharePoint, up from a previous maximum of two. The change took effect on October 31, though Exchange remains capped at two years. Administrators can select recovery windows of three months, six months, or any whole number of years from one to ten. Microsoft's list price is $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content. Extended windows can increase costs by keeping deleted data billable for longer. Switching to a longer recovery window will also not make backups for that period magically available. So no nostalgic trips back to 2016. Wider recovery windows may appeal to organizations that need access to older data, but backups are not a substitute for compliance retention and archiving. Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files. Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements. Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years. Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window. Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan. The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances. Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies." The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed." A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

technology.title: Amazon to flog motors in Britain, but Prime won't deliver
technology.description: Amazon is channeling its inner car salesman as it prepares to flog motors on the UK arm of its online tat bazaar. Amazon Autos will launch in Britain in early 2027, its first expansion outside the US, where it debuted in December 2024. Customers can browse and reserve cars online before completing the purchase with a dealer. Hoping it will be "a nice little earner," Amazon will let punters view real-time dealer inventory, prices, get an instant trade-in valuation, and connect with a local dealer to reserve a car, "all on Amazon." In the US, the service now covers more than 150 cities and offers vehicles from 35 brands. Hyundai is the first announced UK carmaker partner, while dealer group Vertu Motors will list used vehicles. More brands and dealers are due to be confirmed before launch. Hyundai's launch range will include electric, hybrid, and petrol models. "Buying a car is one of the biggest purchases people make, and we think it should feel as simple and transparent as shopping for anything on Amazon," said Matt Nuffort, director of Amazon Autos International. Of course, buying a car isn't quite like adding an air fryer or a memory stick to your basket. How does financing and checkout work for UK buyers? Customers will complete the purchase and paperwork at their chosen dealership. Amazon is not offering financing itself, but buyers can explore financing options via the site, adjusting terms like deposit and duration to see how monthly payments change. technology.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
technology.description: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. Read full article Comments

technology.title: The world's fastest computers have a problem: Keeping the work running
technology.description: Frontier, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's exascale supercomputer, has thousands of processors working together on scientific problems. It also has a surprisingly ordinary way of ruining a researcher's day: one node going down. An uncorrectable memory error can do it, or a maintenance mishap. Scott Atchley , chief technology officer at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, describes technicians accidentally rebooting the wrong node or risking a neighboring node's power supply while working in tightly packed racks. The hardware fault can affect just one node, but a simulation running across thousands of processors can grind to a halt. Then comes a series of questions. How recently did the application save its progress? How much computation needs repeating? And how long before the scheduler lets the job run again? For operators, the challenge isn't just keeping the supercomputer running. It's keeping the science moving. One bad node and everybody suffers On Frontier , a memory error can have an outsized audience. Atchley says uncorrectable double-bit errors in high-bandwidth memory occurred about 1.5 times a day during the supercomputer's early bring-up. Its predecessor, Summit, saw roughly one every two weeks. This sounds like a backward step, until you count the memory. Frontier has more than 16 times as much, giving bad bits considerably more places to hide. Memory isn't the only problem. Problematic GPU firmware can crash a node, and so can a technician rebooting the wrong one. Interconnect faults add another way for a large job to come unstuck. In a tightly coupled simulation using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) simulation, thousands of processes, or ranks, exchange data and participate in collective operations. If one rank disappears, the others cannot carry on as though nothing happened. Clockwork.io CEO Suresh Vasudevan describes a similar dependency in synchronized GPU training. One failed GPU can bring a 1,024-GPU job to a pause. An underperforming GPU can be almost as troublesome: if one participant runs at 80 percent speed, others might have to spend time waiting for it. The bigger the machine, the more ways there are for one small problem to become everybody's problem. How often should you hit save? Since stopping every component from failing isn't an option, researchers need a way to preserve their work. That's where checkpointing comes in. The application periodically saves its state so that, when something goes wrong, the simulation can resume from an earlier point instead of starting from scratch. The catch is that saving progress costs computing time, and doing it too often can become almost as wasteful as losing the work itself. Vasudevan explains this with an example. If writing a checkpoint takes 30 seconds, saving every five minutes consumes roughly 10 percent of computing time. Stretch that interval to 50 minutes, and the overhead drops to about 1 percent. This case kicked off in 2020, when the US Department of Justice claimed entities Huawei operated in America violated federal law. The indictment led to a trial on a dozen criminal matters that has played out over the last three months in the Eastern District Court of New York. The trial ended on Tuesday when a jury found Huawei and three subsidiary companies guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, conspiracy to commit wire and bank fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) and substantive violations of that law, plus money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice’s celebration of the decision says Huawei was found to have stolen Cisco’s source code, after prosecutors showed evidence that “Huawei engineers left Cisco’s notes about the Cisco code, referred to Cisco using its name backwards ‘ocsic’ and described that portions of the code remained as they existed in the ‘ocsic’ code.” Another item of evidence apparently showed a Huawei staffer photographing Fujitsu equipment while wearing a fake employee badge for a company called “Weihua” – cunningly reversing the two syllables of “Huawei.” Another allegation the jury accepted involved Huawei staffers signing a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) ahead of a visit to T-Mobile to inspect a robot the telco created to test mobile devices. technology.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week
technology.description: VMware has issued its third critical security advisory in a week, this time to warn of four critical flaws and address a total of 23 issues. VMSA-2026-0011 landed on November 24, just five days after two other advisories. VMware’s FAQ for the new advisory includes the following remarks: Because of coordinated disclosure and release pipeline timing this VMSA comes on the heels of VMSA-2026-0009, and atop a major holiday in the United States. The security vulnerability landscape is more dynamic than ever; please know that while we acknowledge this timing is not optimal, your ability to operate and maintain a secure environment amidst modern, AI-assisted threats is paramount to us. Make of that what you will as you ponder how and when to patch the four critical flaws, including the 9.8-rated CVE-2026-123903, which allows a malicious actor to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to vCenter, the management tool VMware users rely on to manage hosts and VMs. This is the third 9.8-rated authentication issue VMware has fixed in vCenter since July. Two of the other critical flaws in this new advisory allow an attacker to run code on an ESX host, earning the bugs a 9.8 rating. CVE-2026-123910 makes that possible thanks to a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123911 is a use-after-free vulnerability. The other critical flaw, CVE-2026-123912, can result in a guest escape from VMware’s desktop Workstation and Fusion desktop hypervisors. It’s also present in VMware’s ESX hypervisor, but attackers thankfully can’t escape that product’s sandbox. This one’s easy to mitigate because the problem is in a USB controller that users can turn off. Most of the other flaws require installation of updated software. There’s a little good news in that some of the software updates VMware issued last week include fixes for the newly disclosed flaws. But there are still plenty of fresh fixes to apply, across ten products: ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, VMware tools, Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, the Telco Cloud Platform, Telco Cloud Infrastructure, and the VMware Avi Load Balancer. VMware’s advisory thanks external researchers for finding and reporting most of the flaws. The Broadcom business unit is known to be a member of Project Glasswing, the Anthropic-run effort to use the Mythos model to find flaws that has seen many vendors dramatically increase the number of patches they produce. In past years, VMware has often published considerably more than this year’s 11 security advisories. With five weeks left in the year, perhaps vAdmins need to worry Christmas might also get complicated. ®

technology.title: Nutanix CEO announces gradual departure, intent to complete set of storage links
technology.description: Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami has decided to step down from the job once the company’s board can find his successor. Ramaswami announced his decision on Tuesday and in conversation with The Register said he doesn’t have another job lined up, isn’t sure what he will do next, fancies sitting on boards or advising startups, but will take a break after Nutanix finds its next leader. The CEO moved from VMware to Nutanix in 2020 and characterized his time at the company as writing its “second chapter.” The first, he explained, saw Nutanix focus on hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) and a limited group of workloads, especially desktop virtualization, while struggling to make a profit. In chapter two, Nutanix redefined HCI as “hybrid cloud infrastructure” by enabling its stack to run on-prem or in public clouds, and by adding support for containers alongside VMs. Ramaswami took credit for stabilizing Nutanix’s finances while leading the expansion of its platform and for keeping net promoter scores high while the company grew. The CEO added that Nutanix’s decision to end its devotion to virtualized storage and start to support external arrays was also part of chapter two. Ramaswami said he hopes to expand the number of storage vendors Nutanix supports beyond Dell, Everpure, and NetApp, until it works with all major array suppliers. Chapter 3, he said, will be making Nutanix an AI platform, “by catering to a whole new set of ecosystems.” Ramaswami told The Register he had been thinking about moving on for some time and raised it with the board in recent weeks. In the letter he wrote to Nutanix staff , the CEO said the company's board has begun the search for a successor and said he will remain at his post until a replacement is found and then “continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time.” News of the CEO’s planned departure came on the same day Nutanix announced its Q1 results, which saw 15 percent revenue growth to $772.4 million. The company added 410 customers in the quarter, the slowest growth for several years. Ramaswami said high hardware costs remain “a headwind” for Nutanix, but said the company continues to win customers seeking an alternative to VMware. He also pointed to the largest new customer win for the quarter coming from a financial services outfit that uses Dell external storage, a significant score because two years ago Nutanix could not have competed for that business. Nutanix forecast slightly faster growth for the rest of its financial year, suggesting it is not ready to ride AI’s rocket to riches. Investors knocked about ten percent off the company’s share price in after-hours trading, sending it to around $50, roughly double what it was when Ramaswami took over as CEO, but below $79-plus peaks in late 2025. ®

science.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
science.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."

science.description: Fran Pulido One of the unexpectedly delightful things about becoming a well-known nerd is that other nerds, often with far more interesting jobs than mine, have started hunting me down in social settings to tell me the nerdiest things they know. It almost always ends up being totally fascinating, and only occasionally mildly traumatising. At a kid’s birthday party recently, I got chatting to one of the dads, who happens to be an ear, nose and throat consultant. I asked him if he used robotics for his surgeries. He said no, then proceeded to mime what he actually did instead. There followed a series of alarmingly enthusiastic slashing motions, like a scene from a horror movie, while in the background a group of 9-year-old girls sat quietly painting. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Professor Hannah Fry’s column Sign up to newsletter But the most bizarre thing about that conversation wasn’t the surgeon’s graphic re-enactment, it was what he went on to say about the totally ridiculous, illogical design of the human throat and what it tells us about the path of evolution. The story starts by noticing that the human body (if you ignore all the unimportant bits hanging off the sides like limbs) is essentially just one giant tube. Topologically, this makes perfect sense. Back in the earliest days of animal life, some organisms tried a flat design, like a pancake, with digestion done on one side. Others tried a little pocket, with the same opening serving as entrance and exit. But the one-way tube proved to be the most successful, because it allowed our ancestors to process their last meal while eating their next. Those early creatures would travel through the world mouth first, which is why the sensory equipment evolved to be gathered around that end, with a brain nearby to make sense of everything.
